climate_pressure: Climate-related water stress as an aggravating factor in the historical transboundary-basin account.
documented_impact: Pressure on seasonal irrigation-water availability and allocation.
fcv_mediator: Disputed allocations, weak shared information and damaged/lossy canal infrastructure.
possible_consequence: Risk of cross-border disputes; the source's Aspara account describes diplomacy/accounting as helping avoid violence, not climate inevitably causing violence.
alternative_explanations: Water-demand decisions, crop choice, infrastructure losses, allocation rules and bilateral institutions independently shape disputes.
uncertainty: Historical qualitative study, not causal attribution, current conflict incidence or measured efficacy of mediation; national drought probabilities are not conflict probabilities. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: The study reports public diplomacy, transparent accounting and basin dialogue as prevention capacities in the Aspara case; effectiveness is not independently estimated.
compact_statement: In the historical Chu–Talas account, climate-related stress can aggravate allocation, information and canal-management disputes; the Aspara prevention example highlights dialogue/accounting without implying climate determinism.
